summary.intent: Autonomously run the full GSD post-execute-phase ship loop for phase 67 (TEE republish lease-renewer rewrite): verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E gate → CodeRabbit → ship → resolve PR reviews → extract learnings, deciding fix-vs-defer for every finding without user babysitting.
summary.outcome: Phase 67 shipped as PR #585 (feat: rewrite TEE republish as a verify-in-enclave lease renewer) with all gates green: security SECURED (24/24 threats), Nyquist compliant (0 gaps), SDK E2E 2/2 local, CI 26 pass/0 fail, 10/10 review threads resolved (CodeRabbit CLI 16 findings, Greptile 2 P1s, CodeRabbit PR review 7), 4 todos deferred, and 67-LEARNINGS.md (31 items) committed.

repo: tests/sdk-e2e tee-republish suite is a local-only live-stack gate — CI provisions cipherbox_test (not cipherbox) and runs no TEE worker, so the suite must be skipIf(CI)-gated at both the module-level beforeAll and describe block, or it fails CI with 'database cipherbox does not exist'
Root SECURITY.md is a pre-existing tracked GitHub Security Policy (from PR #482) unrelated to GSD's phase-level SECURITY.md — the security auditor correctly never touches it

.planning/STATE.md and ROADMAP.md can drift out of sync with their own frontmatter (STATE.md showed '0/9 0%' progress bar while frontmatter said 7/9 78%; ROADMAP checkbox said 7/8 while all 8 were done) — worth a periodic consistency check
The GSD commit helper can report commit_failed due to 1Password SSH-signing hangs while the commit actually lands — always verify with git log --oneline -1 before retrying

code.finding: getDueEntries only filtered encryptedIpnsPrivateKey non-null, but the mapper dereferenced signedRecord!/keyEpoch! outside the try/catch, so one malformed row aborted the whole batch — fixed by tightening the null-safety filter

Epoch-upgrade write via .update({ipnsName}, ...) lacked tombstoned_at IS NULL and userId scoping, allowing a tombstoned record to receive a re-encrypted key — fixed by adding tombstone/owner/epoch-CAS scope
Added same-sequence publish guard (TEE-02 defense-in-depth) and re-enrollment reactivation so a stale re-enrolled folder rejoins the due-entries batch
signIpnsRecord was dead code (only self-referenced) after the route switched to renewIpnsRecord, with its old JSDoc orphaned above renewIpnsRecord's — removed both
currentEpoch validation needed to reject non-integer/negative values, not just non-finite; also reordered TEE key validation/wrap before IPFS upload to avoid orphaned blobs on failure

beforeAll ran an unconditional information_schema column-drop assertion and DB query that broke in CI (no live TEE stack); fixed with a CI skip guard; also fixed a queue resource leak (missing try/finally close)

workflow: Run independent audit gates (security, validate) as parallel background agents/skills while a build chain compiles, rather than sequentially
Poll long-running background tasks (CodeRabbit, CI, review threads) via backgrounded commands and wait for task-notifications instead of busy-polling in the foreground
Always git fetch + rebase before pushing after PR creation, since github-actions[bot] pushes a chore(release) commit that will reject a plain push
Triage third-party review findings (CodeRabbit/Greptile) against actual code before fixing — at least one CodeRabbit finding was a false positive that would have wasted a fix cycle
Re-run affected test suites (unit + SDK E2E) after every fix batch that touches the publish/write path, since publish-path edits can silently break the E2E round-trip

friction: Commit helper hit the known 1Password SSH-signing false-negative timeout multiple times, requiring manual git log verification each time before proceeding

CI's SDK E2E job failed on first push because the phase's new tee-republish suite (added in 67-08) had no CI guard and CI doesn't provision a TEE worker or the cipherbox DB — required root-cause diagnosis (log pull, CI workflow inspection) before a fix
A background poll for CodeRabbit + Greptile reviews exited 1 due to a transient api.github.com network blip, requiring re-verification that it wasn't a real failure
Tool call surfaced a transient 'API Error: Internal server error' mid-flow with no apparent lasting effect
CodeRabbit and Greptile re-reviewed each round of fix commits, generating new findings that required repeated triage cycles (CLI review → PR review → fix commits → re-review)

One local e2e re-run showed an 18.99s failure that turned out to be a startup-timing flake (BullMQ/tee_key_state race right after API restart), requiring a clean re-run to confirm it wasn't a real regression
